reviews.text: It's a nice game, its just that i liked the demo version more. I don't understand why Normal blocks don't give health; they are just blocks with no stats. Instead, one needs to select specific items for health. Building and strategising how to build to be effective– which was one of the main reasons I like Terratech – is less prominent then before. You dont need to think how build you just place it, wich 'mutes' the terratech. I have beaten the first few level/ bosses without adding normal blocks, just weapons and some of the other things like the additional damage… One of the big fun factors was removed for most of the early game. 90% of the blocks will literally just sit in the inventory and colect dust, unless you might need a single block to extend for a weapon. But I didn't even need to do it to beat the first few rounds; only later with bigger waapons one might to add a small handfull of normal blocks; but most will still just sit in the inventory. Also the controls in the demo felt a bit less sluggish, which was more pleasant than they are now.

没想到制作组这么快就把新作发了出来，[spoiler] 看来TTW（泰拉科技世界）是被放弃了（？） [/spoiler]。在继承前作玩法的情况下，从慢节奏基地铸造，探索升级变更为了快节奏的，经典肉鸽类型，在很多细节方面能看到TT（泰拉科技）的影子。玩家在地图的上按着任务标识，在途中去打怪，收集各类方块去装备自己的载具，中途有小型的存档点可以抽取方块改装我们的载具，操作很简单，就只有 WASD方向键还有一个shift/空格加速，武器是自动射击的，至少现在不用担心会掉件了，不像前代核心炸了就没了，现在载具一个整体有生命值，血条掉没了，就直接死掉了，前期武器少，容易暴毙，到后期看着自己的载具慢慢壮大，武器种类更丰富，清理满屏的敌人还是很爽的，把这个游戏当是一个休闲小游戏来玩，还是很舒服的。

Avoid until the devs learn to implement basic roguelite features properly. The game looks a bit better than the demo and the combat feels mostly the same but almost everything else is a step back. It's like a greatest hits of bad design choices for a roguelike with meta progression: - No block or ban mechanic - the more you progress, the more parts options you unlock, but because you have zero mechanism to control / filter the pool, this just makes the game more RNG-heavy and therefore harder and less enjoyable. You basically have no control over your build at all. - The meta progression is grindy and feels bad because a) unlocking more stuff actually detracts from the experience (see point above) and b) most of the character upgrades are the dreaded '+1% to this or that stat' aka pointless padding - standard blocks don't do anything any more (they use to give you a small HP boost) so you had a reason to pick them up for reasons other than needing something to mount a gun or component on. In the demo this tended to lead to some wacky builds, now it just makes the normal blocks feel like a waste of inventory

I am a huge fan of the survivors genre and especially where something unique can shake up the formula a bit, but shakes it in a way that isn't a slog. TT legion actually does a genuinely great job of trying something unique, and it works. I am generally NOT a fan of "Drivivors" (I just made that up, but survivor titles with a driving movement / physics based angle) - This is one of the rare times I am actually on board. The building angle is easy to learn and the combos are wild enough once you start getting more heavily into the game and unlock other characters. It is also really hard at first (or maybe I suck), less forgiving than a lot of others in the genre - BUT, the progression loop is rewarding enough and worth the grind, at least at first until you start cranking out your skill trees. Lastly, for those on Steamdeck, it is super optimized really well and runs like a dream.

I had hopes for this game but as-is, I quit. The build system is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. - There are 4 archetypes, but as you unlock them, all parts can be present on the loot table. - The more you progress, the more you unlock parts, the less chance to have a weapon / item for your build / archetype - No ban system or synergy one. - Resulting on fully random runs, frustrating, not fun at all. The first two hours are fun, then you progress, then the game is ruined. Too late for a refund! Also: the vehicule controls are not fun at all, if you want to reverse / forward for example it goes randomly on the right or left.

I’ll keep it simple. 1. Mikela’s vehicle is so bad that when you face a tough boss, you can never dodge in time because the vehicle is so slow and unwieldy. 2. The enemies are strong, while my weapons are ridiculously weak. 3. You cannot disable blocks. It has become impossible to obtain good weapons during missions, and you run out of rerolls very quickly, too. 4. The End. It’s actually fun to play, but it is a grindfest of epic proportions; there are upgrades that cost 60k, yet you only earn between 3k and 5k per run. I really like the music, and I like the design of the blocks and vehicles. Speaking of design: why is Mikela’s nose red? A red nose is associated with drunkenness—and in this game, I’m driving a car. I find making fun of that to be utterly undignified. One of my best friends (Christian)—back in our school days—was run over by a drunk driver (he was just 13 at the time). So, this is anything but funny. If you guys were cool, you’d help send a positive message—especially to young players—by slapping a bumper sticker on the vehicles (even if only in the graphics) that reads: "Don't Drink and Drive." You’d be leaving behind a positive message and making a meaningful contribution to the education of young adults. But as it stands, you’re just a bunch of morons out to make a buck with total disregard for the consequences—after all, in this game, the female driver has a bright red nose, and in missions, you literally run enemies over to kill them. Good job; I hope you’re proud of your work.

I have enjoyed every run including the fails, now they have just brought in the ban mechanic, it takes away some of the diluted weaponry pool, giving to a chance for more fun and powerful builds. Each type of vehicle has its own characteristics (the bike is a solid one to master) and each person comes with its own builds and abilities, these combined with a nice array of weaponary makes for such a great survivors style game. I am a promoter over on Twitch and have gotten into survivor style games pretty deeply recently and can say this is one of much better replay ability ones I've played. I was only given 1 additional key to give away (wish I could have given away more as the game is incredible) I have put a request in to the developers to allow me access to more chances to run/promote this game with giveaways included.

I feel like a lot of the negative reviews are people with skill issues. But the game could do a better job at communicating why you failed... I was iffy on the game before unlocking the 3rd character (Sam), who is likely severely overpowered, but that helped me actually learn how the game works as Sam is extremely forgiving. The more I think about it, the 3rd map and Sam are really good for figuring the game out. It's a snow planet and all of the things that will damage you are red/orange and they're easier to see, and Sam himself gains invulnerability during dash, so you have more time to process everything. After figuring out what actually damages you, how to gain exp and get and place and CHOOSE blocks effectively, the other characters also became a lot more fun. Anyway, the game is perfectly fine for an auto roguelite thingy with placing blocks, and the limitations of the vehicle builder mode are adequately challenging. (Block attachment points, firing angles and so on) Also it works perfectly on linux

第二关那只蛆恶心的要命，近战简直没法玩，而且因为模型的关系非常容易被它的头卡住，然后就是口器抽血 经验值在全部天赋升完就没有用了，但是还是在地图中的某些建筑中可以获得，浪费时间，浪费资源建筑。建议可以用来换一些消耗品。比如每场战斗都比较容易抽中什么类型的武器 这游戏幸运值简直没什么用，少了没效果，多了堆不起来，因为加幸运的部件非常难抽到。 这游戏没有大地图，只有小范围的地图。问题所有图的地形不是一马平川的，经常需要绕道。然后它有几个地图任务是在限制时间内完成突击任务。然后每个突击任务都是随机位置，运气不好刷在地图的两端，还被山围着……尤其是冰川，经常照着指示发现走到死胡同（在山的另一边），然后一路上全是减速的冰。 忘了，还有个腐化方块，也是刷在图里随机位置，小地图上只有靠得足够近才会标注。然后地图任务里至少有4个是和腐化方块相关的 每个公司的徽章，原来是增加局内经验掉落率的。后来改成了更容易刷到相应公司的部件（而且这个所谓的更容易也没什么感觉）。问题是你是什么公司的载具就能“只能”拿到那个公司的徽章。有两个问题，一，我是A角色，我觉得B公司部件用得顺手，但是B公司的徽章我拿不到；二，又不是说你是A公司的，装了A公司的部件有什么额外奖励，到最后还是混搭更优。这破东西还要占1X4的空间 犁这玩意没什么用，还非常容易抽到，伤害又低得要死。简直是武器中的垃圾选项，在高难度只能二选一的时候尤甚。 在选择部件的时候，不能把选择部件最小化。不方便观察已经安装过哪些部件，还有没有空间安装大家伙 第一个角色简直废物，被动是冲刺可以把人撞晕，然而冲刺时不可射击，敌人就晕一小会，你冲过头还没转过来就醒了。特点是可以刷新的次数多，然而多一倍也挽救不了。因为部件太多，很多部件（比方说犁）是三天两头刷到……再刷一遍还在那，真心恶心 LV3的沙漠地图，那个回10000血的地图任务。是认真的吗？？首先，哪怕是每秒回10点血，都需要1000秒，17分钟，而且每秒回4点血的部件那么容易拿的吗？？LV3的地图一次箱子只有2个选项！！就算利用暴击击杀即回血的特性，你还得保持损血状态，因为你满血它所有的回复量就是以0计了。以高难度的伤害来说，你很难保证掉血但又不死的状态：要故意掉点血，不小心就GAME OVER了。上次尝试在回了99XX的情况下BOSS死了。 这个制作组，也就泰拉科技做的还行。其他两个衍生都一言难尽……挺好的IP做成这样。可惜STEAM不能拉黑制作组……

First time I'm posting a review for a game after having a Steam account for 20+ years... and for good reason. This game might be fun initially, but its late game is so laughable that it doesn't deserve the investment of your time. The final character you unlock is extremely weak. So weak that there's no point playing it without spending your collected resources to level up its baseline stats. But that's the problem: you're just investing in losing for the sake of not being pigeonholed into a weak build. Given enough time, the character will become stronger and able to last longer... but it will have very little to do with skill. Just the ability to sit there and lose, collect enough resources, level up, and last a bit longer. It's a deeply unsatisfying loop, and it shows you just how cheesy the mechanics defining this game truly are. 15 hours in, I've uninstalled, and I'm never coming back. Cheers.

Okay, 66hrs and a negative review. Why? I use survivor-style games as a way to watch/listen to YouTube/podcasts because it's unintrusive enough that I don't get distracted mid-sentence. There are some more comprehensive negative reviews out there but the thing that finally got me to uninstall as opposed to "maybe they will fix it in another update" is the final planet. In a game about cars and speed, having the shield-rammer enemies is communicating that I should take this level slow. Even when I did, they were the main reason I died because the camera is so zoomed in I rarely got enough time to react to them showing up. That's just one planet, though, okay. When bosses show up they shove you in a circular arena. Again, game about cars, they restrict your movement. I don't understand the logic. Early game is quite fun. Progression always is, but when you start to stall badly because of the difficulty spikes, the cracks start to show. The game didn't have banish at the start so that was a pain, but then they added it in and even then the RNG is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful I could never, ever get the build I wanted. Flak with AoE boost? That happened something like twice and I still died to shield-cars and bosses that you have to kill from a disatance. Jean-Pierre being tanky and able to withstand multiple hits means nothing if I can't kill the bosses because they will delete both your shields and your health. Late game often feels like you're driving in a quagmire. Perhaps they might do somehting to fix the RNG, but between that and the awful, awful corrupted pieces that 9 times out of 10 offer you something that is completely counter-productive (yes, I have 4 flaks and missile launcher (all explosive damage), and one Sirroco (energy damage)... and you will give me a piece that does 50% energy damage, -75% explosive, and -50 armour... this happened multiple times. It's like the game is reading my build and doing everything to **** me over. If I wanted those odds I would play XCOM.) I don't really think I ought to be giving this game more of my time. The end game so tedious it becomes an endless repetition with no reward. I guess I'll need something else to watch YouTube to.

太好玩了，五星推荐，找到小时候搭积木的感觉，各种各样的武器组合，割草类的杀杀杀，有挑战的boss站，再加上随机的又爱又恨的魇团模块，非常适合喜欢创意建造的轻度肉鸽玩家体验。 超200种模块自由组合，从"乐高废铁"到"科技猛兽"，个性化战车建造空间极大，最大取决于你的想象力，搭配冲刺加速与自动武器可形成独特战斗风格。满屏激光爆炸特效营造炫酷场景，中期战车成型后"冲撞喷火"的爽感突出。 优化的非常到位，对电脑配置要求不高，核显都可以畅玩。 有几个小建议： 一是保存玩家每局生成的战车，可以进行3D浏览，可以分享。 二是加上自定义模式，随便玩家用多少模块都没关系，也可以用自定义战车玩生存模式。 三是尽快出新的地图和人物，4个人、3张地图完全不够玩啊，还可以全是水的星球、气态星球、石头星球、机械星球等等等等。

This is one of those games I can't believe someone made. It's Istrolid but 3D, it's Lego Mad Max, and it's a Blast Corps roguelite! TerraTech Legion, in concept, is way too good to be true. It's such an impossible premise to pull off that it sounds like a scam. Nobody's even trying to make a game like this. Now here comes the crazy part - it's not a scam! They actually made this game! The graphics are weirdly great, not that it matters. There are so many different weapons and whatnot to use, and they don't have to be tediously unlocked. You start out with the full bucket of knockoff Legos to draw in the RNG. The environments are extremely destructible. The framerate stays consistently high even with like a hundred enemies on screen, explosions, the whole nine yards. You get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of bonus crates, at least at the start of each level, so you really don't have to wait to start experimenting with your vehicle's design. And its systems are so much... better than its balance. Everything's got like twice the health it should have and three of four vehicle's starting weapons suck. There's a really longwinded skill tree for each character that only sometimes powers you up enough to matter. They had to buff the starting character with a recent patch, but she's still basically made of glass. The other three's vehicles usually get stuck at their default size and can't have many weapons because they can't select the standard type of structural block in bonus crates. Also there's only 4 characters and 4 stages. This game gets an 8.5 out of 10. Like, it almost makes it into my Steam favorites list. If they fix that stuff I'm complaining about it'll probably be a perfect game.

I don’t think I’ve ever played a game where the “just one more round” urge felt less like hopeless addiction to the loop and more like desperately clinging to the hope that there might be something more beneath the surface. TerraTech Legion isn’t bad- not by any stretch. It runs smoothly and executes its core design competently. The real issue is that what it delivers simply isn’t as fresh or captivating as the box may suggest. If someone asked me whether it was any good, they’d get a hesitant shrug and a lukewarm “It’s… okay.” In a genre where standing out is notoriously difficult, TerraTech Legion makes a genuine effort. You play as a vehicle rather than a character. Movement is tank-style instead of directional. Combat demands more involvement than most survivors-likes. While firing is automated, smart positioning, manual aiming, and well-timed boosts are crucial to winning fights. The selling point is the vehicle-building system, which lets you scavenge parts from the battlefield and loot crates to reshape your rig’s layout on the fly. In that respect, it succeeds at differentiating itself from the crowd, yet even then it often feel disappointingly skin-deep. The appeal of a strong survivors-like is the way steady unlocks and discoveries snowball into wild, off-the-rails experimentation. This is where TerraTech Legion struggles most. Despite being built around customizing and arming your own vehicle, its progression rarely opens up truly creative paths. Instead of “anything goes” chaos, you mostly get “somewhat more interesting” at best. You choose from four characters and four planets. Each planet functions as a distinct arena filled with unique environmental hazards, while each character offers a different mechanical flavor: one centers on recharging energy barriers, another phases through damage with a special boost, a third is slippery and thrives on indirect combat, and the fourth... ... is the girl you start with. The problem is that once you’ve picked your character, upgrades rarely transform how you actually play them. The handful that vaguely do only appear deep in the tech tree. While there’s a wide selection of blocks, most weapons and modules within the same category behave very similarly. Your big decisions often boil down to which direction you want your guns facing, whether they're melee or ranged, and which damage-type buffs you’ll chase. For example, you can pick laser, ballistic, or precision turrets, but that choice mostly just tells you what upgrades to hunt rather than changing your playstyle in any meaningful way. Vehicle construction is a neat concept on paper, but it never becomes the creative outlet you might expect. You aren’t engineering a truly functional machine. Weight distribution barely matters as long as the wheels touch the ground. Instead, it feels more like a spatial puzzle: slotting the parts you’ve acquired into limited chassis space in order to maximize weapon coverage and damage output while leaving room for future growth. That puzzle can be genuinely satisfying during the learning phase, but it quickly turns into repetitive busywork. Once you’ve cracked the optimal layout patterns, you spend each construction phase reshuffling blocks to squeeze in one more module, secretly wishing there was a way to automate the process. Even the “corrupted” blocks, which sound like wild wildcards, add only modest variety. For every genuinely exciting piece, you get another that simply trades one stat for another: “X does more damage but Y is weaker.” There’s something here I want to love. The game flirts with a genuinely cool idea but never fully capitalizes on it. Don’t get me wrong, there is fun to be had. It's just that while some players will find the loop addictive; others will find it monotonous. The truth is that how it feels at hour one changes very little by hour ten or twenty, even after you’ve unlocked the flashier weapons and modules. There are no thrilling synergies to discover, no fast-forward button for the slower runs, and no hidden surprises waiting to blow the game open. If you’re curious, grab the demo and give it a spin. Just don’t expect it to evolve into something truly wild.
